speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) to date, how many ex-offenders have been hired under the Jobs Growth Incentive (JGI); (b) what sectors have they been employed in, in percentage terms; and (c) what steps will be taken to ensure that the ex-offenders will be fairly treated as employees after the end of the 18-month salary support period under the JGI.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Member asked how we will ensure that ex-offenders will be fairly treated after the wage support of 18 months ends.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The JGI is designed such that employers have to shoulder part of the cost of hiring of the worker.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: If the worker, whether an ex-offender or not, proves his value to the company, it serves and it is in the best interest of the employer to keep him on its workforce even after the JGI support has ended.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Otherwise, the employer would have wasted expense and months of effort in training the new hire and risk losing a skilled worker to competitors.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Programmes are available to support employers to train their new hires.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: With respect to ex-offenders placed by YRSG, YRSG provides additional support to them and their employers to facilitate their transition from prison to the work environment.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: A career coach is assigned to the ex-offender for up to 12 months.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The career coaches work closely with ex-offenders and their employers to provide work-related support and resolve issues together.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: However, employers’ business circumstances and manpower needs are constantly changing.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Not all employers will be able to retain every single worker.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Workers who need assistance can approach Workforce Singapore for career matching services.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Ex-offenders can also reach out to YRSG, regardless of whether they are currently receiving YRSG’s assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Any employee that experiences unfair treatment can approach the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP), which will investigate into such complaints.
